title: NTA UGC NET English Full Mock Test #19
subtitle: 100 Questions · 200 Marks · Post-2018 NTA Pattern · Zero Answer Bias (25 A/B/C/D) · Reading Comprehension (Q91-100)

items.title: Mock #19 · Q1
items.stem: Most of the titles of Aldous Huxley’s novels are taken from various literary works. Match the titles of his novels with the works from which they have been borrowed : I. Brave New World A. Blake’s The Marriage of Heaven and Hell II. The Doors of Perception B. Marlowe’s Edward II III. Antic Hay C. Wordsworth’s “The Tables Turned” IV. Those Barren Leaves D. Shakespeare’s The Tempest The right code according to the key is :
items.explanation: Aldous Huxley derived his novel titles from literature: Brave New World (1932) quotes Miranda in Shakespeare's The Tempest [I-D]; The Doors of Perception (1954) borrows from William Blake's The Marriage of Heaven and Hell [II-A]; Antic Hay (1923) quotes Christopher Marlowe's Edward II [III-B]; and Those Barren Leaves (1925) quotes William Wordsworth's "The Tables Turned" [IV-C].

items.title: Mock #19 · Q2
items.stem: Lord Curzon used the report of Indian Universities Commission of 1902 to:
options: centralize school education under a Director-General of Education.
give representation to Indians in policy making.
items.explanation: Lord Curzon used the findings of the 1902 Indian Universities Commission to exert strict governmental supervision and centralize colonial education. This policy led directly to the establishment of the central office of Director-General of Education to oversee schooling standards across British India.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q3
items.stem:
Which of the following is not connected to postmodernism ?
(A) Self-reflexivity
(B) Industrialisation
(C) Magic Realism
(D) Absolutism
(E) Hybridity of Styles
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Postmodernism is characterized by self-reflexivity (A), magic realism (C), and hybridity of styles (E), while rejecting absolutism (D) and the grand narratives of modern industrialisation (B); thus (B) and (D) are not connected to postmodernism.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q4
items.stem:
Who among the following is not
associated with the translation of the
Bible ?
items.explanation: John Wycliffe, William Tyndale, and Miles Coverdale all produced landmark English translations of the Bible, whereas Sir Thomas Browne (1605–1682) was a seventeenth-century meditative prose writer famous for Religio Medici and Hydriotaphia, Urn Burial.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q5
items.stem: Find out the correct sequence of the publications of the following books:
options: India : An Area of Darkness; India : A Wounded Civilization; India : A Million Mutinies Now; A House for Mr. Biswas
A House for Mr. Biswas; India : An Area of Darkness; India : A Wounded Civilization; India : A Million Mutinies Now
A House for Mr. Biswas; India : A Million Mutinies Now; India : An Area of Darkness; India : A Wounded Civilization
India : A Wounded Civilization; A House for Mr. Biswas; India : An Area of Darkness; India : A Million Mutinies Now
items.explanation: V. S. Naipaul's major works listed here appeared in the chronological order: A House for Mr Biswas (1961), An Area of Darkness (1964), India: A Wounded Civilization (1977), and India: A Million Mutinies Now (1990).

items.title: Mock #19 · Q6
items.stem:
Ted Hughes's poem 'The Thought-
Fox' is

I.
About Thought as Fox

II.
About the Fox as Thought

III.
About the process of writing
poetry.

IV.
About Thought entering the
poet's brain like the Fox
emerging from darkness.

Find
the
most
appropriate
combination according to the code
options: I, III and IV are correct
items.explanation: In Ted Hughes's famous poem 'The Thought-Fox' (from The Hawk in the Rain, 1957), poetic inspiration ('Thought') is imagined as a fox emerging from the dark, snowy woods into the poet's mind, serving as a self-reflexive metaphor for the act of writing poetry ('The page is printed').

items.title: Mock #19 · Q7
items.stem:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion (A): Understanding the meaning of any cultural form would not simply locate it within a specific culture.
Reason (R): Cultural forms are best studied in terms of how these fit into the intersection between different cultural networks.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
items.explanation: Because cultural forms sit where cultural networks intersect, their meaning cannot be tied to one culture alone, so R explains A.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q8
items.stem: The phrase “loud colour” is an example of
items.explanation: Synaesthesia is a rhetorical figure and sensory crossover in which one sense modality is described in terms of another, as in describing visual appearance through auditory perception in "loud colour."

items.title: Mock #19 · Q9
items.stem:
Miguel de Cervantes's inimitable Don Quixote, foreshadows metafictional moorings when
the novelist,
(a)
says that the first chapters of the narrative are recreated from the Archive of La Mancha
(b)
says that it is a faithful rendering of a Catalan text in Spanish
(c)
says that part of it has been translated from the Arabic by the Moorish author Cide
Hamete Benengeli
(d)
says that he is rewriting the history of a medieval knight altering the heroic vein with
a farcical mode
The right combination according to the code is
items.explanation: Miguel de Cervantes anticipates postmodern metafiction in Don Quixote (1605, 1615) by claiming that the opening eight chapters were compiled from records in the Archives of La Mancha (a) and that the remainder was translated from an Arabic manuscript by the Moorish historian Cide Hamete Benengeli (c).

items.title: Mock #19 · Q10
items.stem: A 'curtal sonnet' consists of
items.explanation: Invented by Gerard Manley Hopkins and used in poems like 'Pied Beauty' and 'Peace,' a curtal sonnet is a curtailed 11-line (ten-and-a-half-line) sonnet consisting of a six-line stanza followed by a four-and-a-half-line stanza ending in a tail-piece.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q11
items.stem:
Match the column:
(A) A House of Mr. Biswas
(B) An Area of Darkness
(C) India: A Million Mutinies now
(D) A Bend in the River
I. 1979
II. 1961
III. 1964
IV. 1990
items.explanation: V. S. Naipaul published the novel A House for Mr. Biswas in 1961 (A-II), the travel narrative An Area of Darkness in 1964 (B-III), India: A Million Mutinies Now in 1990 (C-IV), and the novel A Bend in the River in 1979 (D-I).

items.title: Mock #19 · Q12
items.stem: A Subaltern perspective is one where
options: Power-structures define and determine your command of language and language of command in an uneven world
You don't know what your 'story' is, how to deal with a 'story' and therefore you are forced to put stereotyped situations in it to please your listeners
The politically dispossessed could be voiceless, written out of the historical record and ignored because their activities do not count for "Cultural" or "Structured
You begin to see how we live, how we have been living, how we have been led to imagine ourselves, how our language has trapped as well as liberated us
items.explanation: Developed from Antonio Gramsci's writings by the Subaltern Studies collective and Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak, the subaltern perspective focuses on politically dispossessed and marginalized groups whose voices and agency are erased from elite colonial and nationalist historical records.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q13
items.stem:
Which of the following statements are true about 'cyberfeminism' ?
(A) Women are not demanding material and social space
(B) It interrogates the patriarchal nature of the new Information and Communication Technology (ICT)
(C) It is a negotiation with the contemporary culture's extensive informatization
(D) Virtual environment does not provide greater freedom to women
(E) Women are unable to appropriate the maternality of cyberspace
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Cyberfeminism critically interrogates the patriarchal structures embedded in Information and Communication Technologies (B) and negotiates women's agency within contemporary culture's extensive informatization (C), making (B) and (C) Only correct.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q14
items.stem: In which play, other than Julius Caesar, has Shakespeare depicted the Romans better than the Roman writers themselves have done?
items.explanation: Among the options, only Coriolanus is a Roman play, and it is praised for its Roman portrait.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q15
items.stem:
Arrange the following works in the chronological sequence of their year of publication:
A. Matthew Arnold’s Culture and Anarchy
B. Robert Burton’s The Anatomy of Melancholy
C. P. B. Shelley’s Defence of Poetry
D. Thomas Hobbes’ Leviathan
E. Walter Pater’s Studies in the History of the Renaissance
items.explanation: The chronological order is: Robert Burton's The Anatomy of Melancholy (1621), Thomas Hobbes's Leviathan (1651), P. B. Shelley's A Defence of Poetry (written 1821, published 1840), Matthew Arnold's Culture and Anarchy (1869), and Walter Pater's Studies in the History of the Renaissance (1873). This yields the sequence B -> D -> C -> A -> E.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q16
items.stem:
Who has defined a poet in the following words:

“The poet, described in ideal perfection, brings the whole soul of man into activity, with the subordination of its faculties to each other according to their relative worth and dignity.”
items.explanation: In Chapter XIV of Biographia Literaria (1817), Samuel Taylor Coleridge famously defines the ideal poet as one who 'brings the whole soul of man into activity' through the synthetic and magical power of the secondary Imagination, fusing disparate elements into an organic whole.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q17
items.stem:
Assertion (A) : Characters in novels are people whose secret lives are visible or might be
visible. We are people whose secret lives are invisible.

Reason (R) : Even when novels are about wicked people, they can solace us; they suggest
a more manageable human race, they give us the illusion of seeing clearly and of
power.

In the light of the statements above
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
items.explanation: Both statements come directly from Chapter 3 ('People') of E. M. Forster's Aspects of the Novel (1927). Forster argues that because novels make characters' secret inner lives visible—unlike real life where others remain opaque—even stories about wicked people comfort us by making humanity seem comprehensible and manageable.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q18
items.stem:
E.M. Forster uses some recurrent
images in A Passage to India. Pick
the odd one out
items.explanation: In E. M. Forster's A Passage to India (1924), the wasp, the stone, and the terrifying echo of the Marabar Caves are major recurring symbolic images. 'Thunder' ('What the Thunder Said') is a central motif of T. S. Eliot's The Waste Land rather than Forster's novel.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q19
items.stem:
Identify the correct order of the publication of DH. Lawrence's works:

A. Rainbow

B. Kangaroo

C. Women in Love

D. Sons and Lovers

E. The Widowing of Mrs. Holroyd

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: The chronological publication order of D.H. Lawrence's works is: Sons and Lovers (1913, D), the drama The Widowing of Mrs. Holroyd (1914, E), The Rainbow (1915, A), Women in Love (1920, C), and Kangaroo (1923, B).

items.title: Mock #19 · Q20
items.stem:
Which of the following critics are associated with Frankfurt School of German Intellectuals:
A. Walter Benjamin
B. Luara Mulvey
C. Travis Henderson
D. Max Horkheimer
E. Leo Lowenthal
items.explanation: Max Horkheimer, Walter Benjamin, and Leo Löwenthal were prominent theorists of the Frankfurt School's Institute for Social Research, pioneering Critical Theory and cultural critiques of mass society. Laura Mulvey is a contemporary feminist film theorist, and Travis Henderson is the protagonist in Wim Wenders's film *Paris, Texas*.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q21
items.stem:
Match List I with List II:
List I (Poet) — List II (Poem)
A. Stephen Spender — I. Cargoes
B. W. H. Auden — II. Consider
C. John Masefield — III. Adlestrop
D. Edward Thomas — IV. The Pylons

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A - I, B - II, C - III, D - IV
A - II, B - I, C - IV, D - III
A - IV, B - II, C - I, D - III
A - III, B - IV, C - I, D - II
items.explanation: Stephen Spender wrote the 1933 poem 'The Pylons' (A-IV), W. H. Auden wrote 'Consider' (1930, B-II), John Masefield wrote 'Cargoes' (1903, C-I), and Edward Thomas wrote 'Adlestrop' (1914, published 1917, D-III).

items.title: Mock #19 · Q22
items.stem: Who in his preface to Joseph Conrad’s The Secret Agent makes the following remark? “the achievement of modern art is that it has ceased to recognize the categories of tragic and comic or the dramatic classifications ‘tragedy’ and ‘comedy’, and views of life as tragicomedy.”
items.explanation: In his 1926 preface to the German edition of Joseph Conrad's The Secret Agent (1907), German author Thomas Mann remarked that modern art abandons rigid categories of tragedy and comedy, viewing human existence essentially as tragicomedy.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q23
items.stem:
Identify the correct pairs :
(A) The Boyfriend — Juliette Banerjee
(B) Nude Therapy — Margaret Chatterjee
(C) The Other Woman and Other Stories — Dina Mehta
(D) The Yankee and the Yogi — B. G. Siddarth
(E) Prejudice of Ages — Vera Sharma
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
items.explanation: Dina Mehta authored The Other Woman and Other Stories (1981, C), B. G. Sidharth wrote The Yankee and the Yogi (D), and Vera Sharma wrote The Early Bird and Other One-Act Plays including 'Prejudice of Ages' (E); The Boyfriend is by R. Raj Rao and Nude Therapy by Juliette Banerjee, making C, D and E correct.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q24
items.stem:
Identify the gynocritics in the following list :

I.
Alice Jardine
II.
Elaine Showalter

III.
Sandra Gilbert
IV. Kate Millett

The right combination according to the code is
items.explanation: Elaine Showalter (II) coined the term 'gynocritics' in 'Toward a Feminist Poetics' (1979) for feminist criticism focused on women as writers, a practice exemplified by Showalter's A Literature of Their Own (1977) and Sandra Gilbert (III) and Susan Gubar's The Madwoman in the Attic (1979).

items.title: Mock #19 · Q25
items.stem:
Chronologically arrange the fictional writings of Margaret Atwood?
A. The Edible Woman
B. The Handmaid’s Tale
C. The Blind Assassin
D. Lady Oracle
E. The Robber Bride
items.explanation: Margaret Atwood's novels appeared in the following chronological order: The Edible Woman (1969, A), Lady Oracle (1976, D), The Handmaid's Tale (1985, B), The Robber Bride (1993, E), and The Blind Assassin (2000, C), making A-D-B-E-C the correct sequence.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q26
items.stem:
In comparative philology and sometimes in modern phonology, what is the term used to refer to the deletion of a vowel
within a word?
items.explanation: In historical phonology and prosody, 'syncope' denotes the loss or elision of one or more sounds (especially an unstressed vowel) from the interior of a word, such as pronouncing 'every' as 'ev'ry' or 'medicine' as 'med'cine.'

items.title: Mock #19 · Q27
items.stem:
Statement I: The book The Life of the Drama was written by Eric Bentley.
Statement II: The book The Life of the Drama highlights the lives of certain seminal twentieth century dramatists.
In the light of the statements given above, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement II is true but Statement I is false
items.explanation: Statement I is true and Statement II is false: The Life of the Drama (1964) was written by critic Eric Bentley, but rather than being a collection of biographies of twentieth-century dramatists, it is a theoretical analysis of dramatic elements (plot, character, dialogue, thought, enactment) and genres.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q28
items.meta: Unit IX: Literary Theory Post World War II
items.stem: The author of “The Politics of Translation” and translator of Mahashweta Devi’s “Standayini” is:
items.explanation: Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak translated Mahasweta Devi's Bengali short story "Standayini" as "Breast-Giver" (in In Other Worlds, 1987) and authored the seminal essay "The Politics of Translation" (published in Outside in the Teaching Machine, 1993), analyzing translation as an intimate, ethical, and political act.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q29
items.stem:
Which statements rightly define or describe 'utopia' and 'dystopia'?
A. Sir Thomas More's Utopia (1516) is an essay in four books.
B. Sir Thomas More was the first to apply 'Utopia' to literary genre when he named his imaginary republic Utopia
C. Thomas More's Utopia was originally written in English.
D. Orwell's Nineteen Eighty Four and Aldous Huxley's Brave New World are dystopian/anti-utopian texts.
E. More's Utopia was translated into French, German and Spanish by Ralph Robinson.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Sir Thomas More coined and applied 'Utopia' (Greek for 'no-place' / 'good-place') to his imaginary island republic in 1516 (B), and George Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four and Aldous Huxley's Brave New World are canonical dystopian/anti-utopian novels (D). More's Utopia was written in Latin in two books (not in English in four books) and was translated into English by Ralph Robinson in 1551, making B and D only the factually true statements.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q30
items.meta: Unit X: Research Methods and Materials in English
items.stem: Who among the following has written the poem, “Jejuri”?
items.explanation: Jejuri (1976) is a sequence of thirty-one poems by bilingual Indian poet Arun Kolatkar that won the Commonwealth Poetry Prize in 1977. The cycle documents a skeptical, irreverent modern visitor's experience at the pilgrimage town of Jejuri in Maharashtra.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q31
items.stem: Match the Graham Greene novel with its setting : List – I I. The Ministry of Fear II. The Third Man III. The Power and the Glory IV. The Quiet American List – II A. Vienna B. Mexico C. Vietnam D. London
items.explanation: The correct novel settings for Graham Greene are: The Ministry of Fear (1943) takes place in Blitz-era London [I-D]; The Third Man (1950) is set in postwar divided Vienna [II-A]; The Power and the Glory (1940) portrays religious persecution in 1930s Mexico [III-B]; and The Quiet American (1955) is set in Saigon during the First Indochina War in Vietnam [IV-C].

items.title: Mock #19 · Q32
items.stem:
Anna Barbauld, Laetitia Elizabeth London, Charlotte Smith, Mary Robinson and Felicia
Hemans are
options: women poets of the Romantic period
items.explanation: Anna Letitia Barbauld (1743–1825), Charlotte Smith (1749–1806), Mary Robinson (1757–1800), Felicia Hemans (1793–1835), and Letitia Elizabeth Landon ('L.E.L.', 1802–1838) were all prominent British women poets of the Romantic period.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q33
items.stem:
Which two titles from among the following deal with issues related to the institutionalisation of English in post-independence India?
(a) Provocations
(b) Professing Literature
(c) The Lie of the Land
(d) The Muse Unchained
The right combination according to the code is
items.explanation: 'The Lie of the Land' (Sunder Rajan, ed.) and 'Provocations' deal with English studies in India. 'Professing Literature' and 'The Muse Unchained' concern the US and Britain.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q34
items.stem: Jacques Lacan posits three 'orders' which structure human existence. In the list that follows : Identify the one that is not included by Lacan
items.explanation: French psychoanalyst Jacques Lacan posited three fundamental psychoanalytic 'orders' or registers that structure human subjectivity: the Imaginary, the Symbolic, and the Real. While the Unconscious ('structured like a language') is central to Lacan's thought, it is not one of the three orders.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q35
items.stem:
Arrange the following novels in the correct chronological order of their publication-
A. So Many Hungers
B. All About H. Hatter
C. Music for Mohini
D. Waiting for the Mahatama
E. Kanthapura
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: The chronological publication order of these Indian English novels is: Raja Rao's Kanthapura (E, 1938), Bhabani Bhattacharya's So Many Hungers! (A, 1947), G. V. Desani's All About H. Hatterr (B, 1948), Bhabani Bhattacharya's Music for Mohini (C, 1952), and R. K. Narayan's Waiting for the Mahatma (D, 1955), giving E, A, B, C, D.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q36
items.stem: The author of Black Skin, White Masks is
items.explanation: Martinican psychiatrist and anti-colonial philosopher Frantz Fanon wrote Black Skin, White Masks (Peau noire, masques blancs, 1952), applying psychoanalysis and phenomenology to examine the internalized inferiority and psychological alienation inflicted on Black people by white colonial racism.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q37
items.stem:
Assertion (A) : In the Absurd plays of Pinter and Beckett, lack of communication seems to be a predominant theme.
Reason (R) : Existentialist philosophy had a tremendous influence on the dramatists of the period, nihilism and meaninglessness of life taking a front seat.
In the context of the two statements, which one of the following is correct ?
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
items.explanation: Both statements are true and (R) explains (A): in the Theatre of the Absurd (Beckett, Pinter), the breakdown of language and communication directly reflects postwar existentialist anxieties over alienation, nihilism, and the meaninglessness of human existence.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q38
items.stem: Who has coined the term “Onto-Theology”?
items.explanation: In post-structuralist literary theory, Jacques Derrida famously utilized and popularized the term 'onto-theology' in *Of Grammatology* (1967) to critique the Western metaphysics of presence, which historically grounds meaning in an ultimate transcendent origin or deity.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q39
items.stem:
Which three of the following plays were written by Sanskrit dramatist Bhasa?
A. Carudatta
B. Ratnavali
C. Urubhanga
D. Malavikagnimitram
E. Karnabharam
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Carudatta (Daridra-Charudatta, A), Urubhanga ('The Shattered Thighs', C), and Karnabharam ('Karna's Burden', E) are classical Sanskrit plays attributed to Bhasa. Ratnavali (B) was written by King Harsha, and Malavikagnimitram (D) was written by Kalidasa.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q40
items.stem:
Where Sir Thomas Wyatt adapted
Petrarch
and
Petrarchanism
to
English sounds and metres, Survey's
verse tends to look back beyond
Petrarch to the
items.explanation: As noted by Andrew Sanders in The Short Oxford History of English Literature, while Sir Thomas Wyatt adapted Petrarchan sonnets to English rhythms, Henry Howard, Earl of Surrey, looked back beyond Petrarch to classical Latin verse—most notably translating Books II and IV of Virgil's Aeneid into English blank verse.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q41
items.stem: Match List - I with List - II. List - I (Text) List - II (Author) (A) The Collaborator (I) Amandeep Sandhu (B) The Garden of Solitude (II) Shahnaz Bashir (C) Roll of Honour (III) Siddhartha Gigoo (D) The Half Mother (IV) Mirza Waheed Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The correct matches of contemporary South Asian novels to their authors are: Mirza Waheed wrote The Collaborator (2011) [(A)-(IV)]; Siddhartha Gigoo wrote The Garden of Solitude (2011) [(B)-(III)]; Amandeep Sandhu wrote Roll of Honour (2012) [(C)-(I)]; and Shahnaz Bashir wrote The Half Mother (2014) [(D)-(II)].

items.title: Mock #19 · Q42
items.stem:
Which famous elegy closes with the following lines ?

"In the deserts of the heart/Let the healing fountain start,/In the prison of his days,/
Teach the free man how to praise."
options: Verses on the Death of T.S. Eliot
items.explanation: These trochaic lines conclude the third and final section of W. H. Auden's famous modern elegy 'In Memory of W. B. Yeats' (written in February 1939), affirming the redemptive, life-affirming power of poetry amidst the approaching darkness of World War II.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q43
items.stem:
Which of the following writers do not exclusively belong to the eighteenth century ?
(A) Oliver Goldsmith
(B) Thomas Gray
(C) Robert Southey
(D) William Cowper
(E) Charles Lamb
items.explanation: Robert Southey (1774–1843) and Charles Lamb (1775–1834) are key British Romantic authors whose major literary works appeared in the 19th century. Oliver Goldsmith, Thomas Gray, and William Cowper died in or before 1800 and belong exclusively to the eighteenth century.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q44
items.stem: Who among the following praised Chaucer's translation of Roman de la rose?
items.explanation: Fourteenth-century French poet Eustache Deschamps praised Geoffrey Chaucer's Middle English translation of the Roman de la Rose (The Romaunt of the Rose) in a famous ballade, hailing him as 'grant translateur, noble Geffroy Chaucier' (great translator, noble Geoffrey Chaucer).

items.title: Mock #19 · Q45
items.stem:
Chronologically arrange the fictional writings of R.K. Narayan in order of their publication?
A. The Vendor of Sweets
B. The Bachelor of Arts
C. The English Teacher
D. The Guide
E. The Financial Expert
items.explanation: R.K. Narayan's novels were published in the following chronological sequence: The Bachelor of Arts (1937, B), The English Teacher (1945, C), The Financial Expert (1952, E), The Guide (1958, D), and The Vendor of Sweets (1967, A), resulting in B-C-E-D-A.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q46
items.stem: 'Stand up, young woman … and tell me what sort of a barbarous people your country folk are, where child-murder is become so commonplace as to require the restraint of laws like yours.' The queen in Scott's The Heart of Midlothian is referring to a strange Scottish law according to which if a woman
options: secretly gives birth to a child and the child is missing and she has not confided to anyone about her pregnancy, she is considered guilty of infanticide
gives birth to a child and the child is missing, she is considered guilty of infanticide
gives birth to a child and the child is missing and she has not confided to anyone about her pregnancy, she is considered guilty of infanticide
gives birth to a child and kills the child and she is guilty of infanticide
items.explanation: In Sir Walter Scott's The Heart of Midlothian (1818), Queen Caroline refers to the harsh 1690 Scottish Concealment of Pregnancy Act under which Effie Deans is condemned. The law decreed that any woman who concealed her pregnancy and could not produce her newborn child was presumed guilty of infanticide.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q47
items.stem:
Assertion (A) : The Waste Land ends in a flurry of random allusions.
Reason (R) : Because it reflects the trajectory of Eliot's own divided life and the hallmark of modernist primitivism.
In the light of the two statements above, which one of the following is correct ?
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
items.explanation: The Waste Land concludes ('What the Thunder Said') with a dense montage of multilingual fragments ('These fragments I have shored against my ruins') (A is true), but these allusions are not merely a biographical reflection of 'modernist primitivism' as claimed in (R) ((R) is false).

items.title: Mock #19 · Q48
items.stem: Who among the following is exclusively associated with diary writing in English?
items.explanation: Restoration naval administrator Samuel Pepys (1633–1703) is famously associated with diary writing in English for his secret shorthand diary kept from 1660 to 1669, recording the Plague, the Great Fire of London, and Restoration life.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q49
items.stem:
The Greek word ‘polis’ refers to-
A. Social Structure
B. Political Structure
C. Legal Structure
D. City State
E. Barbarians
items.explanation: In ancient Greek political thought, the word polis denoted both an independent, self-governing city-state (D) and its formal political structure and citizenship body (B).

items.title: Mock #19 · Q50
items.stem: According to Longinus, the sublime has the following features except
options: It is the essence of all great poetry and oratory
It valorises a special use of language
It is interested in the usual rhetorical goal of persuasion
It is a matter of reader-response
items.explanation: In On the Sublime (Peri Hypsous), Longinus explicitly contrasts the sublime with ordinary rhetorical persuasion: whereas persuasion merely convinces a controlled listener, the sublime transports (ekstasis) the audience out of themselves with irresistible, lightning-like power.

Eliot's 'The Metaphysical Poets' (1921, E).

items.title: Mock #19 · Q57
items.stem:
Given below are two statements :— Assertion (A) and Reason (R):

Reason (R) : Cultural Studies aim to understand Culture in all its complex forms and to analyse the Social and Political context within which it manifests itself.

options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
items.explanation: Assertion (A) is false because Cultural Studies explicitly rejects treating culture as an isolated aesthetic object divorced from society and politics. Reason (R) is true: Cultural Studies examines culture in all its complex forms alongside the social and political power structures in which it operates.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q58

items.explanation: Colombian Nobel laureate Gabriel García Márquez is the preeminent master of Magic Realism, brilliantly weaving supernatural elements into realistic historical settings in novels such as One Hundred Years of Solitude (1967).

items.title: Mock #19 · Q80

items.explanation: In epistemology and literary theory (associated with Richard Rorty and Stanley Fish), anti-foundationalism rejects the existence of any universal, objective ground of truth outside historical frameworks, holding that what counts as 'fact' or 'truth' depends on the interpretive assumptions of each theory or community.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q91
items.stem:
Read the poem and answer the questions that follow (71 – 75) :

The Voice

Woman much missed, how you call to me, call to me,
Saying that now you are not as what you were
When you had changed from the one who was all to me
But as first, when our day was fair

Can it be you that I hear ? Let me view you, then
Standing as when I drew near to the town
Where you would wait for me : yes, as I knew you then,
Even to the original air-blue gown!

Or is it only the breeze, in its listlessness
Travelling across the wet mead to me here,
You being ever dissolved to wan wistlessness
Heard no more again far or near ?

Thus I; faltering forward,
Leaves around me falling,
Wind oozing thin through the thorn from norward
And the woman calling.

items.explanation: In the opening stanza of 'The Voice' ('Woman much missed, how you call to me... Saying that now you are not as what you were / When you had changed... But as first, when our day was fair'), Hardy establishes a stark temporal contrast between the desolate present ('now') and their bright past ('then').

And the woman calling.

Identify the special sound effect in the line iven : Wind oozing thin through the thorn from
norward...
items.explanation: In the penultimate line 'Wind oozing thin through the thorn from norward', Hardy creates an evocative soundscape through alliteration of the dental fricative /θ/ ('thin through the thorn') and nasal sounds, mimicking the whistling chill of the north wind.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q95
items.stem:
Read the poem and answer the questions that follow (71 – 75) :

The Voice

Woman much missed, how you call to me, call to me,
Saying that now you are not as what you were
When you had changed from the one who was all to me
But as first, when our day was fair

Can it be you that I hear ? Let me view you, then
Standing as when I drew near to the town
Where you would wait for me : yes, as I knew you then,
Even to the original air-blue gown!

Or is it only the breeze, in its listlessness
Travelling across the wet mead to me here,
You being ever dissolved to wan wistlessness
Heard no more again far or near ?

Thus I; faltering forward,
Leaves around me falling,
Wind oozing thin through the thorn from norward
And the woman calling.

What longing does the speaker voice ?
options: longing for reunion in the other orld
longing for physical union in the town here they used to eet
longing for physical union in the present
longing for a return to the town here they used to eet - o O o -
items.explanation: Throughout the lyric, the grieving speaker expresses an agonized longing to physically view and be reunited with his lost wife as she was in her vibrant youth ('Let me view you, then... Even to the original air-blue gown!'); the ambiguity between physical and spiritual reunion led UGC to award marks to all.

items.title: Mock #19 · Q96
items.meta: Unit IV / Unit VIII: Prose & Criticism
items.stem:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option :

The town belonging to the colonized people, or at least the native town, the negro village, the medina, the reservation, is a place of ill fame, peopled by men of evil repute. They are born there, it matters little where or how; they die there, it matters not where, nor how. The native town is a hungry town, starved of bread, of meat, of shoes, of coal, of light. The native town is a crouching village, town on its knees, a town wallowing in the mire. The look that the native turns on the settler is a look of lust, of envy…. The colonized man is an envious man. And this the settler knows very well… It is true, for there is no native who does not dream at least once a day of setting himself up in the settler's place.
(From Frantz Fanon's The Wretched of the Earth)

To Frantz Fanon, the 'Negro' village is
(1) the worst face of apartheid
(2) a protected area
(3) a place of moral and physical degradation
(4) a special village with its own amenities.
items.explanation: In the passage from The Wretched of the Earth, Fanon depicts the segregated native town or 'negro village' as the starkest manifestation of colonial racial division/apartheid (1) and a site of severe moral and physical deprivation (3).
